title: Marple: Scalable Spike Sorting for Untethered Brain-Machine Interfacing
problem: Spike sorting from electrophysiological signals is challenging at scale: software solutions require high-power GPUs and operate post-hoc, while hardware solutions sacrifice accuracy and support only up to 128 channels.
motivation: Advances in neural recording probe technology enable thousands of channels, requiring efficient portable spike sorting solutions for real-time brain-machine interfaces.
method: Marple splits the work into two stages. First, a fixed hardware piece (the frontend) filters noise from incoming electrical signals from brain electrodes in real-time. Next, a flexible software component (the backend) uses machine learning to determine which neuron created each electrical spike, rather than comparing each spike to stored reference patterns. The system compresses how it stores these patterns by 8-11x, which frees up enough memory to handle thousands of channels instead of being limited to 128.
key_novelty: A compression technique for stored reference patterns that reduces memory use by 8-11x, enabling spike sorting on thousands of electrode channels rather than 128.
contributions: Identification of template memory storage as critical bottleneck in spike sorting systems
Novel compression mechanism achieving 8-11x memory reduction
Scalable hardware architecture supporting 1000s of channels versus 128 in prior hardware solutions
First ML-based replacement for template matching stage in spike sorting pipeline

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 79mW projected in 7nm at 10K channels peak activity

baselines: hardware spike sorters (prior, up to 128 channels)
limitations: Paper does not provide detailed accuracy comparison against state-of-the-art software spike sorters or evaluation on real neural recordings; implementation is projected, not yet realized.
primary_theme: Scalable hardware spike sorting for portable brain-machine interfaces
